Maya Patel: Heads-up — on the Gemma->Llama3 bring-up I saw a consistent drop on summarization BLEU at scale when we enable rotary harmonics adaptation. Not huge but reproducible across seeds.
Samir: Hmm, is this the harmonic phase remap landing change from the conversion script?
Maya Patel: Yes, two changes: we applied a per-head phase-scale (to preserve headwise freq) and used a vectormap remap for vocab offsets. Both landed in the same PR.
Jin Park: Can you paste the failing eval run?
Maya Patel: Paste below (trimmed):
```
# eval summary
model: gemma->llama3-conv-v2
quant: int8-static
promptset: summarization-small
seed: 42, 43, 44
bleu: baseline 28.4 -> conv-v2 26.9
rougeL: baseline 34.1 -> conv-v2 33.2
latency: +3% tail
```
Samir: Interesting — int8 static could amplify small phase misalignments. Did you try float16?
Maya Patel: Yes, fp16 matches baseline within noise. The regression shows up after quant and with long prefixes (>512).
Kai: Could be kvcache key collisions if token ids shifted by vectormap. Any token-id histogram diffs?
Maya Patel: I ran a tokenid diff on a 10k sample: about 0.7% tokens differ mapping compared to previous converter — mostly punctuation and rare diacritics.
Jin Park: That might explain small hallucination-ish drops in summarization. Those tokens can anchor boundary conditions for ROUGE.
Samir: Two experiments to run: (A) swap to old vocab remap + new harmonic scaling; (B) keep new vectormap + disable harmonic per-head scale.
Maya Patel: Started A locally, single seed: bleu -> 28.1 (so almost recovered). B queued on CI.
EvalBot: CI job queued: 7743220001 (A/B sweep: seeds 1-3, int8,int4,fp16), ETA ~ 45m
Kai: Also try disabling KV prefix caching in the int8 run — if the kvcache index calc assumes previous token ordering, cache hits could be misaligned after remap.
Maya Patel: Good call, adding that to the matrix.
Jin Park: For long-term: we should add a token-preservation test to the tokenizer conversion pipeline — assert <0.1% remap on top 100k tokens, and flag punctuation spikes.
Samir: Agreed. Add a small eval in onboarding: 1) histogram diff, 2) per-token top-10 embedding cosine for common tokens to detect projection drift, 3) end-to-end quality smoke.
Maya Patel: I'll open a follow-up PR with the regression-bisect notes + temp revert for vectormap until we validate.
Kai: If A recovers, we can reintroduce vectormap as an opt-in with a compatibility flag so Dedicated customers aren't affected. :thumbsup:
Maya Patel: Update: A finished on my machine, BLEU 28.2, int8 latency back to baseline. Uploading logs to the thread.
Samir: Nice. Keep CI run results here when EvalBot finishes.
EvalBot: CI results for 7743220001: int8(A) passed seeds 1-3, int8(B) still regressed, int4 shows larger variance. Artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/7743220001/
Maya Patel: Conclusion: harmonic scaling is fine; vectormap remap causes subtle token-id shadowing under quantization. Will revert vectormap by default. Thanks all.
Jin Park: Add a note to the model-onboarding checklist about running quant-sensitivity across tokenizer diffs.
Kai: Filing a tiny RFC for opt-in vectormap and tokenizer preservation checks.
Maya Patel: Thanks — closing loop here.
